input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.2 imposes a Company-payable Termination Payment on any termination by us, measured as half of the excess of the preceding twelve months' Net Sales over $800,000 and payable in eight quarterly instalments. That is a liquidated amount payable by the Customer that is untethered from our fees (30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month under Section 3.1) and can far exceed three months of fees, so it fails the fallback cap as well as the preferred position of no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties. No other Customer-payable penalty, late-payment interest or minimum fee appears in the document; Section 1.6 (termination "without penalty" for late go-live) runs in our favour. We propose the preferred position by removing the payment formula while preserving the defined term, so the retained "if any" mechanics in 4.2(b)-(c) remain internally consistent.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Zero out the Company-payable Termination Payment so no liquidated damages or penalties are payable by the Company.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have removed the Company-payable Termination Payment formula so that no termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty is payable by us on termination; the existing "if any" mechanics in Section 4.2 remain harmless. If a termination charge is essential, we could accept one capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
